Kai: Heads-up — hitting a new KV symptom I'm calling "ghosting" during longctx runs. Memory climbs steadily and small prefix entries keep getting re-instantiated across requests, causing fragmentation and a spike in page evictions.

Kai: Repro on CI longctx: heap +1.8GB over 30m, kv_fragmentation ~0.27, kv_evictions/sec up ~5x. Flamegraph: http://internal.perf/fg/2798

Ana: Can you paste the exact load command you used? Trying to reproduce locally.

Kai: Sure:
```\nmake e2e-longctx\ntools/run_load --profile kv --seq 2048 --clients 120 --duration 30m
```

Megan: Noted — we started getting similar traces after the kernel-selector change (v2.14 -> commit abc123). Could be interaction between new batching windows and prefix lifetime.

Patrick: Perf bot output from the run:
```\nkv_pages_evicted: 4.2/s -> 23.1/s
kv_fragmentation_ratio: 0.12 -> 0.27
kv_residency_ms (median): 120 -> 930
```

perf-bot: Alert: kv fragmentation > 0.2 on node-3 (auto-tagged)

Ana: Two hypotheses: 1) key design is too session-unique so identical logical prefixes don't share entries; 2) eviction heuristics treat these small prefix pages as low-pop hot items so they bounce.

Kai: For (1) we're currently composing key = tenant_id | session_nonce | prefix_hash. Session_nonce purpose was to avoid stale leakage between sessions, but if it's reused or overly granular we lose cross-request reuse.

Megan: Could we switch to a two-tier key space: stable_prefix_key = tenant_id|prefix_hash (global) + session_key TTLed for session-scoped state? That would allow reuse for common prefixes while preserving per-session data.

Patrick: Also saw that when batching window increased, KV access patterns spread across more contexts so the hotset skews — makes fragmentation worse. Maybe eviction policy needs neighbor-aware compaction.

Kai: Proposed quick mitigations:
- Use stable_prefix_key for read-mostly prefixes with a short residency boost (micro-LRU pinned for N accesses).
- Keep session-scoped keys but TTL them aggressively (e.g., 30s) and prefer in-place update instead of creating new allocation.
- Add neighbor-aware compaction: when freeing a page, attempt to coalesce small adjacent entries into a compacted page (cheap compaction pass when eviction ratio crosses threshold).

Ana: Implementation notes: stable_prefix_key changes keying semantics. We need to ensure no correctness regressions for writes (e.g., session-specific mutations). Maybe add a flag on keys indicating "shared-read-only" so writes still create session-prefixed entries.

Megan: Agree. For safety we should gate behind a feature flag and canary in one pool. Canary plan: 2 pods on canary pool, 5% traffic, monitor mem/evictions/latency. Roll back if kv_fragmentation_ratio increases or latency SLO breached.

Patrick: Experiment plan I propose:
- baseline run 1h collect mem/evict/residency
- enable stable_prefix_key + TTL session
- run same load, compare metrics (A/B)

Kai: I'll prototype keying change and the in-memory flag mapping. Ana — can you add metrics: `kv_key_type` (stable|session), `kv_residency_ms`, `kv_compactions`?

Ana: On it. Also adding trace points around allocation path to catch blob churn.

Megan: I'll own the canary rollout and experiment harness. Will also wire the flamegraph link into the dashboard.

Patrick: Small perf tweak idea: when kernel-selector picks wide batching windows, add a backpressure hint to the KV manager so it raises TTL for frequently reaccessed prefixes temporarily. That should reduce churn during high-concurrency bursts.

Kai: Good call. We'll prototype that as an independent knob so we can test kernel-window + kv-ttl coupling.

Megan: ETA: canary ready tomorrow afternoon. I'll post results + dashboard link.

Ana: ETA for metrics + trace points: EOD today.

Kai: Thanks — owners noted: Megan(canary), Ana(metrics), Patrick(dashboard/policy), Kai(prototype). We'll sync async; if canary shows improvement, we'll schedule rollout and follow-up compaction work.

Megan: :thumbsup: 

perf-bot: Noted run ids: 2798765432 (baseline) -> 2798765480 (canary)

Patrick: Quick note — add a unit test for keying: ensure read-only shared keys never expose session-scoped write state.

Kai: Good call. I'll add tests with mocked sessions.

Megan: Closing loop later with numbers. If anyone sees unexpected correctness issues ping me @channel.

Ana: Will do. 

Kai: Thanks team — keeping this thread pinned while we run canary.
